title: Whole-source pair counts removed 106 of 132 local failure ambiguities in eight selected worm map models
abstract: We tested whether whole-source constraints remove local uncertainty in three-target failure in eight partial worm brain maps. In a model with independent, equal-probability shared release at synaptic sites, we tested all 22,049 target triples from 763 source-map cases with 3 through 10 retained targets. Local counts allowed 132 ambiguous triple intersection counts. Integer optimization over all nonempty target subsets left 26 ambiguous triples after all source target-pair counts were fixed. The number fell to 22 when the histogram of retained targets per site was also fixed. Thus whole-source pair constraints removed 106 local ambiguities. The largest remaining silence-probability interval width was 0.08192 at assumed site failure probability 0.8. All 528 endpoint witnesses passed integer constraints; 406 small-case optimizer checks matched exhaustive enumeration. These are conditional model results, not measured release or neural activity. The fanout cap, selected panel, partial maps, one species and ideal release assumptions limit transfer. Code, aggregate evidence, a figure and pinned retrieval steps support reproduction. External site records and record-level alternatives are excluded.

display.caption: Whole-source pair constraints removed most local ambiguity in selected sources with 3 through 10 targets. A site-size constraint removed four more cases. Probability widths use assumed failure probability 0.8. Maps are separate animals; connected points do not show an estimated age trend.
